key_insight: Rare-earth silicates are promising third-generation environmental barrier coatings because they balance CMAS and water-vapor resistance with compatible thermal expansion, but performance depends strongly on phase, composition, and coating microstructure.
engineering_relevance: The review guides EBC design for ceramic matrix composites by linking phase stability, thermodynamics, and microstructure to durability under extreme service environments.
method: Clarifies phase-formation rules and their thermodynamic/crystallographic basis
Compares single-component and multicomponent silicates, separating bulk from plasma-sprayed coating behavior
Summarizes corrosion mechanisms and multi-objective design strategies for harsh environments
evidence_signal: The evidence is a literature review synthesizing bulk and coating studies on phase stability, thermal properties, and corrosion resistance rather than new experimental data.
watch_item: Plasma-sprayed coatings may deviate substantially from bulk ceramics due to SiO2 loss, amorphous phases, porosity, and segregation, so bulk-derived phase/property rules may not directly transfer.
paper_title: Advances in Rare‐Earth Silicate Environmental Barrier Coatings
